AutoDisconnect.desc: Write script to automatically disconnect you based on some conditions.

AutoBucket.desc: Automatically uses water bucket when you fall. Module only searches water bucket on your hotbar. Don't rely solely on this module, since you can die just because of bad ping. Don't fall on waterloggable blocks like leaves, since your water cannot be placed on top of such blocks. Module doesn't check if you already are falling into water. There was plans to add other items like cobweb or slime block.

AutoFish.desc: To start automatic fishing, throw fishing bobber once. To stop you can pull bobber manually or disable it.

AutoTotem.desc: Automatically puts Totem of Undying into your offhand slot, if this slot is empty and you have totem in your inventory.

AutoDrop.desc: Drops gargabe from inventory. Use Scripting to assign key bind. Example:

ContainerButtons.desc: Show additional buttons for containers UI (chects, barrels, ender chests and so on).

AutoEat.desc: Automatically consumes item held in offhand. Can be useful for afk farms.

AntiRespawnReset.desc: Prevents accidental right clicks on beds/respawn anchors.

AutoCraft.desc: Add items you want to auto craft. To start autocrafting enable module and open Crafting Table GUI. Algorithm: If you have enough ingredients to craft at least 1 item, module performs shift+click on recipe (if resulting item is stackable), or simple click (if resulting item is non-stackable). If you don't have enough items, module tries to craft missing ingridients. It can go recursively. For example, your recipe needs sticks, but you have logs. Module will craft planks from logs, and then sticks from planks. Module performs shift+click on resulting item(s). If your inventory is full, module will stuck here. You can safely close Crafting Table GUI. Module is not smart enough to deal with full inventory. You should better have some free slots before crafting. Module is not smart enough to calculate if you have enough sub-ingredients to craft at least 1 item. Example: you selected Dispenser as item for Auto Craft. You don't have bows/sticks/string in your inventory. You have planks in inventory. Module will craft sticks from planks once (for bow recipe), and stop here.

AutoAttack.desc: Auto Attack makes it so that holding the attack button autoswings the sword, similar to the combat snapshots. Each swing is done right after the attack cooldown is done and thus will always do max possible damage.

BreachSwap.desc: Looks for a breach mace in your hotbar, if you have a breach mace, it will perform an attribute swap with your currently held item and the breach mace

Schematica.desc: Module can only properly place simple blocks, which have only 1 block state. No directional blocks, stairs, slabs and so on.
labels: Treat replaceable blocks as air (e.g. snow, water, grass). Requires rescan.
Air blocks in schematica are always valid. Requires rescan.

AutoHotbar.desc: Automatically refills configured slots on hotbar from inventory if number of items fall below 50% of stack size. Can be useful for AFK farms.

AutoTool.desc: Automatically switches to the best tool right before you start breaking block. "Best" tool is determined by best mining speed. If there is no such tool, it switches to any non-damageable item.

SpearRange.desc: Uses the spear to extend your reach with weapons.

AutoStunner.desc: Automatically disables shield if you have an axe available and the target is holding a shield that would block your attack Module accounts for target look direction

BlockESP.desc: Lines thicker than 1 pixel cost more CPU/GPU resources.

ProjectilePath.desc: Show most likely path of projectiles (Minecraft adds some random to every shot). Displayed path in not precise in close distance, since player shoots projectile from eyes, but module draws path from right hand. This is done to have better visuals, in other case you would just see single vertical line.
labels: Show traces for all projectiles around

LightLevel.desc: Show transparent overlay over blocks where monsters can spawn. Helps you to spawn-proof locations.

EndCityChunks.desc: Highlights chunks where End Cities can generate. Chunk groups 9x9 size will be highlighted with transparent green layers, and center chunks highlighted with yellow. This helps you to move in direction of yellow path moving from one group to another.

EntityOwner.desc: Shows who owns tamable animal. This module was moved under Custom Title System in Entity ESP. Open Entity ESP, search for entity type you want to see owner (for example Animal base class). Check "Custom Title System" and "Show Owner".

FreeCam.desc: You can move camera around and through blocks. Default key F6, but can be changed in options. You can open chests through walls or attack entities.

NewChunks.desc: Uses liquid flows (water and lava) to determine if chunk is newly generated. Chunk status is displayed on Exploration Mini Map. Red squares - old chunks (chunks contains non-source water/lava blocks) Green squares - new chunks (chunk didn't have non-source water/lava blocks, but server sent block update packets with non-source water/lava) Yelllow squares - relatively new chunks (chunk already had non-source water/lava, but new non-source water/lava blocks appeared) Chunk without square - there is no water/lava to guess chunk status

EntityTitle.desc: Overhauls Minecraft default entity title system. Displays titles with static font size with no distance fade out. Use Entity ESP to enable this for specific entities.

KillAura.desc: Automatically attacks entities in range with the current item in hand.

ElytraHack.desc: Allows you to fly with Elytra without rockets.

PigHack.desc: Most servers have protection against big speed increase. However small speed increase may work well.
labels: Allow ride without carrot on the stick

AutoCriticals.desc: Tricks server to think every your attack is critical.

FlyHack.desc: Sometimes if you turn off fly hack close to surface (1-2 blocks) you can take a lot of fall damage and die (even with No Fall enabled). Workaround: before turning off fly hack, fly upwards (even 0.5 seconds can be enough). If you move upwards server resets internal fall distance value and sets it to zero. If you move downwards for a long time server accumulates fall distance, and that's why you take fall damage.

ElytraTunnel.desc: Allows you to fly in nether highways without stucking in holes in ceiling. For example, if ceiling is Y=123, you should enter slightly lower value, for example about 122.8. This module emulates collissions on the client, thus doesn't allow you to reach higher Y.

Scaffold.desc: Automatically places blocks below the player. Module Automatically selects full blocks from your hotbar. It will not select stairs or slabs.
labels: Replace blocks from inventory on hotbar

NoFall.desc: When you are falling fast enough to take damage, it sends information to server that you are staying on the ground. Server uses this information to calculate fall damage. If server doesn't have protection against this usually you take no fall damage.

FastBreak.desc: When you mine block your client sends 2 packets: when you started digging and when you finished. Due to ping problems time difference between 2 packets can differ between client and server. To make block dig rollback more rare server weakens rule, and doesn't check exact time. We can abuse this and always send 2 packets quicker. This hack cannot make "non-instamineable" block instamineable. Instamining has strict check on the server.

Reach.desc: Modify block interaction range and attack range. Kill Aura range setting is not affected by this.

TeleportHack.desc: Use Keybindings to assign keys. Module can trick the server think you are lagging. Second parameter for teleport methods called "repeats" sends your current position packet to server "repeats" times. Vanilla server will reject more than 5 packets sent during single server tick. More packets you send - farther you can teleport. I would not set this more than 5 since any basic anticheat will mark you suspicious, but you are free to set it up to 100. Lowest accepted value = 0.

FakeLag.desc: Emulates network lag. Once you enable this module all packets (server -> client and client -> server) are rejected and stored in buffer. As soon as you disable module all packets from buffer are processed. Your minecraft client receieves all skipped packets from server, and server receieves all packets from client with almost no delay between packets.

Blink.desc: Use Keybindings to assign keys. When enable module blocks all MovePlayer packets (contains position/rotation) send by client. You can continue moving on client, but you stay at original position on the server. Use blink.enable() for keybind. Once module is enabled you have to 2 options. Disable module with blink.disable(); . In this case you will be teleported back to original position and all movement packets will be discarded. Or send movement packets to server with blink.apply() You can use blink.getDistance() to see how far you moved from position you enabled blink. blink.getPackets() - to see amount of captured packets.

InvMove.desc: Allows you to use all hotkeys while different UI screens are active. For example you can move with inventory opened. Doesn't work in Forge version!

AreaMine.desc: Automatically mines blocks surrounding your target block. Activates only if you can instamine target block (when you break block in 1 click, like grass).

ServerPlugins.desc: Use serverPlugins.get(); or serverPlugins.getBukkit(); to scan for server plugins. AntiCheats may disable this approach, in this case these methods return empty array.

HitboxSize.desc: Allows you to extend entities hitboxes. Extended hitboxes are applied only during calculation of target entity and while rendering hitboxes in debug (F3+B).

BedrockBreaker.desc: Breaks bedrock with single button click. Conditions: Any Pickaxe on hotbar (not required, will be used to break pistons) Some amount of pistons on hotbar Some amount of levers on hotbar Some amount of replace blocks (if enabled) How to use: Add bedrockBreaker.process(); to keybinding Target bedrock block Ensure there are 2 empty blocks above or below bedrock Ensure there is 1 free block nearby to place lever and power the piston Press hotkey If something goes wrong you should see system message In this way you can break 1 bedrock by targeting it and pressing hotkey. Or you can use bedrockBreaker.processNearby(); method to automatically break all nearby bedrock blocks at the highest Y level. Doesn't work if your mining speed is so big you instamine pistons.

AntiHunger.desc: Modifies movement packets and tells the server you are not standing on the ground. This cause to lose hunger points slowly than usual. However most anticheats will consider this as flying.

StepUp.desc: Allows you to walk up X blocks height without jumping. By default Minecraft allows you to step up only by 0.5 height for slabs/stairs. Don't use with built-in Auto Jump option.

AirPlace.desc: Allows you to place blocks in the air, not attached to other blocks. Draws cube at the potential location of the block. While module is active use scroll to adjust range. Min/Max range can be configured below.

ArmorOverlay.desc: Display 4 armor slots above food bar.

ShulkerTooltip.desc: Hover mouse cursor over shulker box in inventory to see shulker content.

ExplorationMiniMap.desc: Press Tab to show mini map. Hold Alt while holding tab to show players list. Use mouse scroll to zoon in/out. If you travel long distances (tens of thouthands blocks), this mini map may cause FPS drop on low-end system. Also all sections of map are kept inside RAM and video memory. To clear them from memory just disable/enable.

Fog.desc: Disable all fogs (water, lava, powder snow).

Chunks.desc: Overrides server render distance. Some servers have pretty low render distance, and your game setting is getting overriden. For example, if server set render distance = 6 chunks, that means game doesn't render blocks 6*16=96 distance above or below you. If you select below option, you can see far above/below you (if you have decent Render Distance in-game setting).

StatusEffects.desc: Display status effects above hotbar. Also displays seconds.

Zoom.desc: Allows you to zoom to see distant objects.

WorldMarkers.desc: Add markers to your world so you can see them from any location. For example your base or some farm. Min Distance parameter: if target location is closer than specified value - it is not rendered. You can use it so marker doesn't distract you when you are doing something on this location. You can add/remove markers from scripting by using markers API.

BobHurt.desc: Disables camera rotation when taking damage.

FakeWeather.desc: Once enabled minecraft ignores time and weather change packets from server. Allows you to manually set time or weather on client.

LogoutSpots.desc: Displays location of players logging out spots. If you enable Custom Title System for Player entities in Entity ESP , it can also show names, HP and equipment of disconnected players.

BlockEntityDistance.desc: Render distance for most block entities (chests, signs, beds, banners, etc). By default it is fixed at 64 blocks.

KeyBindingScripts.desc: Write scripts and bind them to ingame keybindings.

BlockAutomation.desc: Write script to place blocks, use items on blocks, break blocks in range. Every game tick module runs your script for all blocks in range. You can get current block coordinates from x , y , z variables. If your script calls blockAutomation.useItem(...); or blockAutomation.breakBlock(...); module will use item and place block, or break block at current coordinates. Some items require player to look in the correct direction to be used. These kind of items send another packet to the server and are not supported by block automation. Example: filling/emptying bucket or glass bottle. If you are unsure if your item can be used from Block Automation try enter FreeCam and use item while looking at another direction.

Exec.desc: Allows you to execute script from chat window. Every chat message starting with single dot is considered as script and will be executed.

VillagerRoller.desc: Automatically places/breaks lectern and checks Librarian trades. Write script to decide when module should stop. Look at villagerRoller.getState() to see current module state and perform correct initial setup.

Tps.desc: Calculates server tick rate based on SetTime packet. You can display TPS by using scripting and Status Overlay. Use method tps.get() → float .

Debugging.desc: Call debug.write("text"); from any script to see logs here. Module keeps either last 100 logs or logs from last second (which is bigger).

Profiles.desc: Create profile with different settings and switch between them. You can use profiles API to switch profiles from scripts. You can use events.onJoinServer from Events Scripting module to automatically load profile based on server and/or Minecraft account.

UserName.desc: Change user name without restarting Minecraft. This is only for pirate servers, it cannot work with Mojang authentication.

ContainerSummary.desc: Shows total number of items inside chests, barrels, etc., including nested shulker boxes. Hold Alt to disable stacks grouping.

LockInputs.desc: Emulate holding keys or lock mouse input.

WorldDownload.desc: Downloads chunks from multiplayer server into your singleplayer world. To start downloading: - Create new singleplayer world (or use existing one) - Enter directory name of singleplayer world save directory (you can find it in "/saves" directory) - Press "Start" button (no need to be logged in multiplayer server) - Start loading server chunks by moving or logging in. - Use Exploration Mini Map to see which chunks were saved to disk (dotted square) - Press "Stop" button (don't forget to Stop before loading singleplayer world!) Module only saves original chunks sent by server. For example, if you loaded chunk, built something here - this will not be saved. You need to unload/load this chunk to save new changes. Note: some servers use custom dimensions, for example for spawn region. In this case region files will be saved into "/dimensions/somename1/somename2/region". You can manually copy region files into root "/region" directory to see them in your single player world.

Reset.desc: This button allows you to reset mod config. Basically it deletes all Hellenic Client related config files, and prevents from recreating them in current session. You have to manually exit Minecraft after this. If you have some useful configurations or scripts, you can backup config files manually by copying them from config directory inside your Minecraft installation. You can also delete config files manually if you want. Remember to always restart Minecraft after this, so mod will start with fresh config. "Reinstalling" mod can't fix any problem. Mod JAR file is static and never changes.

HellenicCape.desc: Shows a cape on your player, and on your elytra too. Only you can see it, other players still see your normal cape. Pick which cape in the Capes tab.
